commands.name: login
commands.summary: Signs in by approving a code from the console. Without an interactive terminal, in two steps: --start, then --wait.
flags: --start: asks for the code and exits 5 with the URL to approve it
--wait: waits up to 90 s for the approval; exits 5 if it has not arrived (call it again)
--dry-run: says what it would do without doing it
--json

commands.name: logout
commands.summary: Revokes the key in use and deletes it from this machine.
flags: --dry-run: says what it would do without doing it
--json

commands.name: whoami
commands.summary: Shows which key the terminal uses, in whose name and in which team.
flags: --json

commands.name: describe
commands.summary: Describes commands, flags, capabilities and exit codes, for an assistant.
flags: --json

commands.name: repo connect
commands.summary: Connects this folder's repo (or --repo) with the GitHub App; a person confirms it in the console. Two steps: --start, then --wait.
flags: --start: asks for the connection and exits 5 with the URL
--wait: waits up to 90 s for the approval; exits 5 if it has not arrived
--repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--dry-run: says what it would do without doing it
--json

--test "…": the test command of the project

--dry-run: says what it would do without doing it
--json

commands.name: project show

--json

commands.name: catalog

commands.name: guide check
commands.summary: Checks .supcoflow/guide.md (or the old guia.md if guide.md does not exist) without publishing it. Exits 3 with a list of errors per line if it is badly formed.
flags: --repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--dry-run: says what it would do without doing it

commands.name: guide publish
commands.summary: Publishes the guide. Uploads the file it read, with its path; --from-github reads the default branch on GitHub instead. Publishing the same guide again returns the same publication (ya_publicada).
flags: --from-github: read the guide from GitHub instead of this clone
--repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--dry-run: says what it would do without doing it
--json

commands.name: guide show
commands.summary: Shows the guide in force, its path and whether it was declared.
flags: --repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--json

commands.name: guide use
commands.summary: Chooses which guide the chat reads: the repo's or the agent's.
flags: --source repo|agent: which guide the chat reads
--repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--dry-run: says what it would do without doing it
--json

commands.name: guide versions
commands.summary: Lists the published versions of the guide and which one is in force.
flags: --repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--json

commands.name: widget
commands.summary: Gives what is needed to put the chat in the app: the package and exact version, the wrapper file (nextjs), the suggested file, the earlier files and the CSP line.
flags: --repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--json

commands.name: install record
commands.summary: Writes .supcoflow/instalacion.json (version 2): with which versions the chat was installed and which file mounts it. Repeating it without changes does not touch it. Exits 4 cambios_sin_commit or archivo_no_versionado if git does not hold the previous one.
flags: --skill version: the metadata.version of the installing skill (semver, required)
--app folder: the app folder, relative to the repo root (default: the root)
--file path: the file that mounts the chat, relative to the repo (no .., not absolute, not a symlink)
--repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--dry-run: says what it would do without doing it
--json

commands.name: diagnose
commands.summary: Checks the installation at no cost, in two groups: installation (sign-in, repo, GitHub App, allowed sites, chat and guide: N of 6) and whether a test could run now.
flags: --repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--json

commands.name: test
commands.summary: Tests the installation end to end: a problem enters through the same door as the chat and ends up as an issue. With --authorize-spend it spends one investigation (up to --ceiling; with the save policy it stops at the saved case and spends nothing). Without --authorize-spend it sends nothing: exits 4 falta_autorizacion with techo_usd, saldo_usd, tope_usd and comprometido_usd. With --authorize-spend it needs --ceiling and --expect-policy, exits 5 with prueba_id; then --wait follows it. Others: 4 prueba_en_curso, techo_distinto, politica_distinta, chat_deshabilitado, requiere_api_key, intento_pendiente; 6 tope_mensual.
flags: --authorize-spend: authorizes the spending of ONE test; needs --ceiling and --expect-policy
--ceiling usd: the ceiling the person saw (never re-read)
--expect-policy investigate|save: the policy it was offered with
--message "…": the text of the test problem (default: a fixed one)
--wait: follows the last test up to 90 s; exits 5 while it runs, 0 with the issue (or saved), 4 if it needs a look
--test prb_…: with --wait, follows that test instead of the last saved one
--repo owner/repo: the repo, if it is not this folder's "origin"
--dry-run: says what it would do without doing it
--json

global_flags: --json: the result as one JSON line on stdout; warnings go to stderr

capabilities.name: read
capabilities.includes: Identity and team, projects, settings, installation state, reading and checking the guide (guide check, guide show, guide versions)

capabilities.name: configure
capabilities.includes: Create or reuse the project, connect the repo, configure and turn on the chat, allowed sites, data agreement, problem policy, publish the guide, choose the active guide (guide use), create and revoke read keys

capabilities.name: test
capabilities.includes: The test up to the issue (spends, within the caps)

capabilities.name: console_only
capabilities.includes: Raise the spending cap, delete the project, turn on the factory, give or remove people's access: only with a console session

capabilities.name: operator
capabilities.includes: Requests, /maquinaria, close runs, the operator factory: never by key, even if the person is an operator
